title: Product and Software Requirements Specification — DK Bond Tracker v2

sections.heading: Objective
sections.body: Replace the macro-enabled Excel bond tracker (`v5.5_40L_Project_Tracker.xlsm`) with a full rebuild: a local SQLite database (one per user, no cloud and no accounts) plus a lightweight Flask web UI as server-rendered HTML with no build step, that reproduces all current behavior (payment ledger, live dashboard, status engine, CSV export) while fixing the Excel/VBA quirks, runs fully offline on any desktop OS, and stays easy to maintain as the data grows.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The current bond tracker is a mini-application trapped inside an XLSM file: VBA rebuilds the dashboard on every open/save (blocking MsgBox), month headers are hardcoded Sep-2025..Feb-2027, the month scan stops at Jan-2031, "Danger" checks only the previous month, errors are silently swallowed by `On Error Resume Next`, and the dashboard is a stale static snapshot between saves. Sharing means sending the whole workbook, and any export to CSV/xlsx loses all behavior. The owner wants an offline, lightweight, shareable, maintainable solution that scales as the portfolio grows. In the rebuild, the status engine replaces the single-month Danger rule: Danger = ANY unpaid past month (D5).

sections.heading: Actors
sections.body:
1. **Primary — Owner (Adi-Mudi):** tracks 15 bonds, records monthly payments, reads the dashboard, exports CSV.
2. **Secondary — Friends (peer users):** receive a copy of the app and run it on their own machines with their own local database; no cloud or accounts.
3. **Tertiary — Spreadsheet/CSV consumers:** people who receive exported CSV files for sharing/printing (read-only, outside the system).

| US-05 | Owner | As the owner, I view a live dashboard (totals, status counts, this-month returns, 83-month history) without opening Excel. | FR-05 | proposed |

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body:
**In-scope:** local SQLite schema (bond master, payment ledger, home_plan) as a per-user local file; Flask local web UI with server-rendered HTML and Excel-like month grid; one-time XLSM import (Excel stays read-only backup); live dashboard queries; fixed status engine; CSV export; quirk fixes from the Excel analysis; owner wish-list features staged in later phases.

**Out-of-scope:** cloud sync, accounts/authentication, mobile apps, network multi-user mode, real-time market data, replacing Excel files retroactively beyond the one-time import (Excel stays read-only backup).

sections.heading: MVP
sections.body:
### MVP Goal

A friend can copy one folder to their machine, run a single launch command, import the existing XLSM (or start empty), record payments in a month grid, and see a live dashboard with correct statuses and CSV export — with Excel no longer required for any daily operation.

### MVP Users

The owner first; then friends running the same folder on their own machines with their own local DB file.

### MVP Requirements

- FR-01, FR-02, FR-03, FR-04, FR-05, FR-06, FR-07, FR-08, FR-09, FR-10, FR-17, FR-18, FR-19, FR-20, FR-21, FR-24

### Explicitly Not in MVP

- Home Plan schedule reproduction (FR-12, Phase 3)
- Watch-list analytics formulas (FR-11, Phase 3)
- Discount / TDS / quarterly-yearly payouts / P&L dashboard (FR-13..FR-16, Phase 4)
- Duplicate-ISN validation hardening and schema decoupling polish (FR-22, FR-23, Phase 2)

### MVP Exit Criteria

Import reconciles exactly (15 bonds, Total Investment 550000.00, Total Till Return 28500.00, Total Balance -521500.00), dashboard reflects edits without any open/save event, every FR-01..FR-24 Phase-1 acceptance test passes, and a clean machine reaches a working dashboard within 1 minute using one documented command.

sections.heading: Phases
sections.body:
### Phase 0 — Foundation

#### Goal
Project skeleton, Python/Flask/SQLite dependencies, test harness, XLSM parser spike (HF-05).

#### Requirements
None (prerequisite only; no FR ids).

#### Acceptance Criteria
App skeleton boots; parser spike reads the real XLSM sheets.

#### Dependencies
Python 3.14 venv; oletools/openpyxl available for parsing.

#### Risks
Formula-vs-static-value mix in sheets (Home Plan) complicates parsing.

#### Out of Scope
Any requirement rows.

### Phase 1 — MVP

#### Goal
Complete Excel replacement: schema, ledger, import, grid UI, fixed status engine, live dashboard, CSV export, quirk fixes, error surfacing, reinvestment free-up.

#### Requirements
FR-01, FR-02, FR-03, FR-04 (incl. color rules), FR-05, FR-06, FR-07, FR-08, FR-09, FR-10, FR-17, FR-18, FR-19, FR-20, FR-21, FR-24.

#### Acceptance Criteria
MVP Exit Criteria (MVP section) all met.

#### Dependencies
Phase 0; original XLSM available as import source.

#### Risks
Import parity with VBA-derived values; status-rule differences vs old behavior must be clearly communicated.

#### Out of Scope
Home Plan, watch-list analytics, discount/TDS/payout-cycle/P&L features.

### Phase 2 — Essential improvements

#### Goal
Robustness: error surfacing polish, duplicate-ISIN validation, schema decoupling.

#### Requirements
FR-22, FR-23; ERR-03, ERR-04.

#### Acceptance Criteria
Duplicate ISN flagged across full bond set; no header-text/position coupling remains; unresolvable current month yields explicit message.

#### Dependencies
Phase 1 schema.

#### Risks
None significant.

#### Out of Scope
New analytics features.

### Phase 3 — Advanced features

#### Goal
Home Plan savings schedule and watch-list analytics reproduction.

#### Requirements
FR-11, FR-12; DATA-03, DATA-04 consumption; ERR-06.

#### Acceptance Criteria
Home Plan reproduces incl. irregular savings (25000, 10000, 0); watch-list formulas (discount, TDS, per-month, qty TL) match Excel outputs.

#### Dependencies
Phase 1 import (fields already landed in DATA-03/04).

#### Risks
Formula/static mix in Home Plan — stored values must be preserved.

#### Out of Scope
Owner wish-list items not yet delivered.

### Phase 4 — Scale and optimization

#### Goal
Remaining owner wish-list plus scale validation.

#### Requirements
FR-13, FR-14, FR-15, FR-16; NFR-11 verification.

#### Acceptance Criteria
Discount, TDS, quarterly/yearly cycles, and Dashboard P&L/ongoing TL value delivered; dashboard < 2s with 150 bonds × 96 months.

#### Dependencies
Phase 1 ledger; Phases 2–3 preferred complete.

#### Risks
Payout-cycle changes touch ledger/status logic — regression tests required.

#### Out of Scope
Cloud, mobile, networked multi-user.

sections.heading: Errors and Edge Cases
sections.body:
| ID | Condition | Expected Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| ERR-01 | Bond beyond old Jan-2031 scan window | Status and rendering still produced; never silently skipped |
| ERR-02 | Zero-value payment in a past month | Treated as unpaid; Danger check applies |
| ERR-03 | Current month cannot be resolved for This Month Returns | Explicit message shown, not a silent 0 |
| ERR-04 | Duplicate ISN in bond set | Flagged across entire bond set |
| ERR-05 | XLSM import failure | Failure reported explicitly, never silently swallowed |
| ERR-06 | Home Plan formula/static mix | Import preserves stored values verbatim |

sections.heading: Constraints
sections.body:
1. Fully offline; no cloud services or accounts (user requirement).
2. Data lives in a single local SQLite file per user (shareable by file copy).
3. Desktop-only for now; browser is the UI (no separate Android/Linux/desktop builds).
4. Python 3.14 environment already exists (`.venv` with oletools).
5. Original XLSM remains as read-only backup; it must not be modified by the tool.
6. Web search was disabled during brainstorming; all requirements trace only to local artifacts.
7. ISO/IEC 29110 basic profile; IEC 62304 safety class A (non-safety-critical tracking tool).

sections.heading: Dependencies and Risks
sections.body:
1. Python + Flask + SQLite availability on users' machines (low risk, standard install).
2. XLSM parsing dependency (openpyxl/oletools) for import — formula/static mix may hide values (medium risk; spike in Phase 0).
3. Behavior change vs old Excel (fixed Danger rule, no MsgBox) may surprise users — communicate in changelog.
4. Friends' machines vary by OS — NFR-3 portability test required.
5. No formal upstream requirements existed; RTM was derived after the fact — the workbook itself is source of truth.

sections.heading: Out of Scope
sections.body:
1. Cloud sync, accounts, authentication.
2. Networked multi-user mode / shared server database.
3. Android/iOS native apps.
4. Live bond-market data feeds.
5. Modifying the source XLSM file.
6. Retroactive rewriting of historical Excel files beyond the one-time import.

sections.heading: Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
1. Import of the real XLSM reproduces 15 bonds and exact totals (SM-01).
2. Dashboard figures change immediately after any payment edit, with no open/save event (SM-02).
3. Status engine flags every unpaid past month; Completed overrides Danger; zero counts unpaid (SM-03).
4. A bond starting Feb-2031+ receives correct status and grid rendering (SM-04).
5. CSV export opens correctly in a spreadsheet application.
6. A clean machine reaches a working dashboard within 1 minute using one documented command (NFR-4).
7. All Phase-1 FR rows pass their verification method with status moving proposed → verified.

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.body:
| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| Bond tracker | The system being replaced: XLSM workbook with VBA dashboard/status engine |
| Ledger | One row per payment (bond, month, amount, paid flag) — the core storage model |
| Month grid | Excel-like view with months across columns, rendered from ledger rows |
| Till Return (K) | Total payments received to date for a bond (Excel column K = SUM of month cells) |
| Balance (L) | Till Return − Maturity Amount (Excel column L; negative = still to receive) |
| Danger / On-going / Completed | Status engine states; Danger = any past unpaid month (fixed rule), Completed = tenure fully paid |
| Watch list | Static analysis sheet with discount/TDS/yield formulas per bond |
| Home Plan | 84-month savings simulation schedule with interest calculations |
| Wish list | Owner's Note-sheet TODO: discount, TDS, quarterly/yearly, P&L, reinvestment free-up |
| PSRS | Product and Software Requirements Specification (this document) |
| EARS | Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax (When/While/… sentence shapes) |

sections.heading: Change Log
sections.body:
- 2026-09-27 — PRD scout team (fr-extractor, nfr-checker, helper-detector, consolidator) + parent merge — initial draft v1.0.0 created from brainstorm notes and doc-code analysis of the actual .xlsm. User decisions applied: FR-04 extended with color rules; NFR-11 numeric target (2s @ 150 bonds × 96 months) confirmed; FR-21 promoted to must/Phase 1; FR-17 + US-03 promoted from wishlist to Phase 1 (owner's "most important feature"); FR-12 + DATA-03 moved to Phase 3.
- 2026-10-30 — v2.0 born-JSON revision superseding the legacy markdown PRD: FR-01..FR-24 carried one-to-one in `prd_items` with confirmed-decision mapping (D1 Flask server-rendered frontend, D2 one-time XLSM import with read-only Excel backup, D3 row-per-payment ledger with UI month grid and live queries, D4 CSV export, D5 fixed status engine — Danger = any unpaid past month, Completed overrides, zero = unpaid; D10 offline-only per-user local SQLite). Legacy quirk fixes retained: visible error surfacing, dynamic month headers with no window limit, always-live dashboard, duplicate-ISIN validation across the full set.

prd_items.statement: The system SHALL store all data in a local SQLite database schema comprising a bond master table, a row-per-payment ledger table (one row per payment: bond ref, month, amount, paid flag), and a home_plan table.
When a user starts the application, the system SHALL serve a Flask web UI locally as server-rendered HTML with no build step, requiring only Python and a browser.
When a payment is recorded, the system SHALL store it as one ledger row (bond ref, month, amount, paid flag) instead of a month column.

When the user opens the month grid, the system SHALL render an Excel-like grid (months across) derived from ledger rows, coloring paid cells green, due cells light red, and status cells red/orange/green for Danger/On-going/Completed.
When the user views the dashboard, the system SHALL compute all figures (portfolio summary counts/amounts, this-month returns, monthly history, status overview) as live queries/views.

When ANY past-month payment is missing (not only the previous month), the system SHALL set status Danger; when payments made >= tenure, the system SHALL set status Completed (overriding Danger); a zero-value payment SHALL count as unpaid.
When the user requests an export, the system SHALL produce a UTF-8 CSV of any displayed dataset (CSV replaces any xlsx export).
When the import script is run, the system SHALL read the source XLSM once and populate SQLite, keeping the Excel file as a read-only backup.
When payments exist, the system SHALL compute Till Return as the sum of paid ledger rows and Balance as Till Return minus Maturity Amount, as queries (never stored).
When import completes, the system SHALL hold all 15 bonds' master fields exactly as in the source workbook.
When the watch list is viewed, the system SHALL reproduce the analytics formulas (discount, TDS, per-month, qty TL, 12-month totals).
When the Home Plan is viewed, the system SHALL reproduce the 84-month savings schedule including irregular savings (25000, 10000, 0).
When a bond has a discount, the system SHALL record and display the discount amount per bond.
When a payout is due, the system SHALL compute and display TDS deduction on payouts.
When a bond's payment type is quarterly or yearly, the system SHALL generate due dates on that cycle instead of monthly.
When the dashboard is viewed, the system SHALL show P&L and ongoing bond total (TL) value.
When a bond reaches Completed, the system SHALL free its principal for reinvestment, and duplicate-deduction rules SHALL apply only to On-going and Danger bonds.
When the current month is beyond a fixed range, the system SHALL still generate grid columns/borders dynamically with no hardcoded Feb-2027 window.
When a bond's payment window starts Feb-2031 or later, the system SHALL still compute status and render its rows (no scan-window limit).
When data changes, the system SHALL refresh the dashboard on the next view without any open/save event trigger.
When an operation fails, the system SHALL surface the error to the user visibly; the system SHALL NOT swallow errors silently.
When a duplicate ISN exists in the bond set, the system SHALL flag it across the entire set (not a partial row range).
When data is read or written, the system SHALL use stable schema keys and SHALL NOT couple logic to header text or column positions.
When payment history changes, the system SHALL recompute the bond status immediately without requiring open/save events.
